A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIDM framework and theoretical questions. Their main text, equations, experiments, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix K report original synthetic-graph and MUTAG correlation experiments, plus DIDM classification accuracy in Table 1.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix M report original synthetic-graph, MUTAG and PROTEINS experiments, alongside the retained DIDM classification result.

M1.justification: The recursive DIDM metric, optimal-transport computation and normalized-sum MPNN updates remain unchanged. Appendix D adds an expressivity-equivalence analysis of an existing message-function formulation, rather than changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's MUTAG and constant/Gaussian-feature SBM experiments, v3 adds PROTEINS and an SBM scenario with community-constant features sampled uniformly from [0,1]. These substantially extend the represented data and feature conditions; the earlier synthetic scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all five graph-metric comparators. However, v3 Figure 4 adds GraphConv to the MUTAG single-network width comparison whose corresponding single-network row in v1 Figure 5 showed only GIN. GraphConv already participated in other experiments.

E3.justification: The reported Gaussian noise schedule changes from (50-i)/50 to (49-i)/49 in Appendix M.2.2. MUTAG depth sensitivity is reported using single-network distances in v3 Figure 5, whereas v1 Figure 3 used maxima over 100 networks. The classification experiment retains its 90/10 split.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands sensitivity evidence through community-constant feature experiments and single-network width/depth analyses on MUTAG and PROTEINS. The original single/maximum/mean comparison survives as Figure 10. The maximum-over-100 depth panels from v1 Figure 3 are no longer reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten random classification splits and identical mean-plus/minus values in Table 1. Single-network and 100-network aggregation analyses already existed in v1; v3 introduces no new confidence intervals, significance tests or seed-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New community-feature and PROTEINS plots substantially expand the reported outcomes, including the GraphConv-versus-GIN distance-preservation finding on PROTEINS. Table 1 is numerically unchanged: DIDM remains 89.47 ± 7.81, and Chen's WL distance remains 91.1 ± 4.3. The added plots provide results under additional conditions, not improved classification accuracy.

T1.justification: v3 adds graphon-signal compactness proofs in Appendix E.3, direct universality in Theorem 7, graph-signal density in Theorem 19, and architecture-equivalence proofs in Appendix D. It introduces explicit feature and formal-bias bounds and replaces v1's class-count generalization argument with Theorem 8's joint-distribution bound, with probability 1-p and explicit uniform Lipschitz/bias controls.

C1.justification: The central expressivity, universality and distribution-free generalization claims remain. The contribution list removes v1's explicit trustworthiness-tool assertion and qualifies approximation of 'any function' as approximation of continuous functions, refining the stated scope without changing the central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 expands the earlier dense-graph and aggregation limitations with density-rescaling qualifications, an explanation of why unnormalized sums fail, and possible mean-aggregation extensions. Appendix M adds a noise-averaging explanation, limits what the classification experiment establishes, and develops the informal random-MPNN observation into a more specific convergence conjecture.

D1.justification: Appendix M newly documents the GIN/GraphConv implementations, including MLPs, batch normalization, skip connections and readout, plus reference-graph selection and SBM block sizes. Section 4 supplies a code-repository link where v1 only promised release upon acceptance, although Section 8 retains that old promise. These are documentation additions, not evidence of architecture changes.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against WL-distance theory, robustness-style generalization bounds, restricted GNN generalization analyses and sparse-graph limit theories. Added discussions involve Chen et al. (2023), Xu and Mannor, Oono and Suzuki, Li et al., Tang and Liu, and Rauchwerger and Levie (2025), beyond relocating the existing related-work section.

P1.justification: The introduction, contributions and experimental explanations are extensively revised. Related work moves to Appendix B, Main Results becomes Theoretical Applications, and the conclusion becomes a Discussion. The appendices regroup proofs and add substantial explanatory structure, while the notation index is revised.

P2.justification: The correlation displays are extensively reorganized, with expanded captions, TMD axis labels corrected to DIDM, separated synthetic panels and added community-feature and PROTEINS plots. Figure 3 moves from the main text to the appendix with a revised panel selection; Table 1 is relocated without numerical changes.

improvement.justification: v3 materially strengthens the central theoretical support through direct graphon-signal compactness/universality proofs and explicit uniform model bounds. Its generalization proof replaces v1's argument assuming N/C expected samples per class with a direct joint-distribution argument. Fuller experimental documentation and clearer limitations also improve assessability. Some summary wording still understates the formal assumptions, and code-release statements conflict, but these residual issues do not outweigh the substantial gains.
